The example below is the **complete** live response (23 tokens on 2026-10-30). Each bridged route appears only while it is live. `ondoTokens` is accepted and ignored.

getQuote.notes: Returns **HTTP 200** on success, as 1Click does. The request below sets **every** field Tidepool accepts (the twelve required ones plus all optional ones); `simulate` is left out because it changes the swap's outcome. The response is a real dry quote. With `dry: false` the response adds `quote.depositAddress`, `deadline` and `timeWhenInactive`, see the live example below. See [Quotes and pricing](/docs/concepts/quotes) and [Swap types](/docs/concepts/swap-types) (full requests and responses for each swap type). Tidepool-only: the optional `simulate` field (`STUCK` or `FAILED`) simulates a stuck or failed swap on testnet, see [Stuck or failed swap](/docs/guides/failure-cases#stuck-or-failed-swap-simulated-outage). Remove it when you move to mainnet 1Click.

getExecutionStatus.notes:
The example below is a real `SUCCESS` swap (5 USDC → wNEAR). See [Status lifecycle](/docs/concepts/status-lifecycle).

**Settlement distinction.** On mainnet, 1Click now settles every swap confidentially on the NEAR Private Shard, so `swapDetails.nearTxHashes` lists only the public shield and unshield transactions ([NEAR changelog, Oct 27, 2026](https://docs.near-intents.org/changelog/entries/2026-10-27-1click-confidential.md)). Tidepool testnet swaps settle publicly on the testnet verifier, so `nearTxHashes` also includes the swap's own hash. This is not a choice by Tidepool: confidential settlement (NEAR Private Shard / Confidential Intents) runs on NEAR's private infrastructure, which isn't exposed to outside builders. Rely on `status` (`SUCCESS` means delivered), not on the presence of a swap hash, so the same code works on both.

submitDepositTx.notes:
Optional. Returns **HTTP 200** and the current status object. Moves `PENDING_DEPOSIT` to `KNOWN_DEPOSIT_TX`; the worker detects deposits on its own either way. For a `depositMode: "MEMO"` quote (NEAR-native origin tokens, Stellar and XRP) also pass `memo` (the quote's `depositMemo`). For a NEAR-native MEMO deposit also pass `nearSenderAccount`, which Tidepool uses to look the transaction up. `/v0/status` takes the same memo as the query parameter `depositMemo`.

**Settlement distinction.** On mainnet, 1Click now settles every swap confidentially on the NEAR Private Shard, so `swapDetails.nearTxHashes` lists only the public shield and unshield transactions ([NEAR changelog, Oct 27, 2026](https://docs.near-intents.org/changelog/entries/2026-10-27-1click-confidential.md)). Tidepool testnet swaps settle publicly on the testnet verifier, so `nearTxHashes` also includes the swap's own hash. This is not a choice by Tidepool: confidential settlement (NEAR Private Shard / Confidential Intents) runs on NEAR's private infrastructure, which isn't exposed to outside builders. Rely on `status` (`SUCCESS` means delivered), not on the presence of a swap hash, so the same code works on both.

400.message: accountId must be a NEAR testnet account id

TidepoolFaucet.notes: Limits: one claim per address every 24 hours across all faucet variants; six per IP per hour. Other chains: send `{"chain":"base","address":"0x…"}` (also eth, arb, sol, stellar, sui; btc and xrp answer 400 with the external faucet to use, since native BTC and XRP are never dripped). Bridged tokens into the verifier: `{"accountId":"alice.testnet","mode":"intents","assets":["sol"]}`. In `wallet` mode `drips` has one entry and `transactions` one transaction per token (all six NEAR test tokens by default); in `intents` mode the transfer is batched into one transaction per six tokens. The 200 sample below was recorded from a live `wallet` drip and is **shortened**: it lists two of the six tokens in `drips` and only the first mint in `transactions`. A full response lists every token (one `transactions` entry per token in `wallet` mode). See [Faucet](/docs/guides/faucet).

bridges.note: Testnet bridges (EVM chains, Solana devnet, Stellar testnet, Sui testnet, Bitcoin testnet4, Zcash testnet and XRP Ledger testnet): trusted relayer run by Tidepool, testnet only.

TidepoolHealth.notes: Cached for 10 seconds. Re-checks the verifier code hash against the build of the `defuse/v0.4.5` tag. See [Live status](/docs/status).

authenticate.notes: The example signs with a throwaway ed25519 key (`raw_ed25519`); the account id is the key's 64-hex implicit account. The `payload` is a JSON string with `signer_id`, `verifying_contract`, `deadline`, `nonce` and `intents`. For `nep413` the same fields go in `payload.message` with `payload.nonce` (base64) and `payload.recipient`. The tokens below are real and expire (access token 1 hour), and belong to a throwaway account with no funds.

refresh.notes: Send the `refreshToken` from `/v0/auth/authenticate`. Real request and response (throwaway account).

getBalances.notes: Needs `Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>` from `/v0/auth/authenticate`. Without `tokenIds` only non-zero balances are listed (an empty account returns `{ "balances": [] }`); with `tokenIds` every requested token is listed, including zeros as below. `tokenIds` takes a comma-separated list. Real response for a fresh throwaway account.

getHistory.notes: Needs `Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>`. Lists swaps where the account is the `recipient`, `refundTo`, sender or signer, newest first. Real response for a throwaway account that created two quotes (a swap quote and an order).

generateIntent.notes: Only for quotes with `depositType: INTENTS` (the deposit address is an intents account). The `intent.payload` is the exact string to sign; sign it with your wallet and send the result to `/v0/submit-intent`. The `deadline` in the payload is about 15 minutes ahead. Real request and response from a live quote.

401.__text: Tidepool does not return this: `/v0/submit-intent` takes no authentication.

submitIntent.notes: Send the signed `intent` from `/v0/generate-intent` as `signedData`. The request below is the real, correctly signed intent for the quote in the generate-intent example. The throwaway signer holds no tokens, so the verifier rejected it: that is the real **400**. The **200** body is the spec's example, because producing a real one would mean transferring funds from a funded account (not done for these docs); it has the spec's fields `intentHash` and `correlationId`; Tidepool also adds `tidepool.txHash` and `tidepool.explorerUrl` (the relayed verifier transaction) to a successful response.
